belief: The more I do for God, the more He loves me.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that the more you do for God the more He loves you, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: A home where affection came through achievement. Church recognition for the most active members. Perfectionism and a drive to prove yourself. Comparing your service with others. Feeling loved only when productive.
teaches: God’s love is not a reward for what you do. Love consists in this: not that we loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son. Christ died for us while we were still powerless and ungodly. Nothing can separate us from God’s love, and nothing you do can increase it. You can serve God with joy, but you cannot earn more of a love that is already complete.
self_statements: God loves me more when I serve more.
If I slow down, God will love me less.
I have to keep proving my love to God.
My worth is measured by my service.
God’s love has to be earned.
errors: Believing God’s love rises and falls with your performance.
Measuring God’s love for you against others’ service.
Picturing God’s love like a parent who rewarded achievement.
Pushing harder and harder to feel loved.
questions: According to 1 John 4:10, who loved first?
When did Christ die for us?
Can anything separate me from God’s love?
Did the prodigal son earn his father’s embrace?
If I could never serve again, would God love me less?
Am I serving to get love or because I have it?
What would serving from security look like?
truth: God’s love for me does not grow with my service. He loved me first, sent His Son for me while I was powerless, and nothing can separate me from His love. I can serve Him joyfully because I am already fully loved, not to earn more love.

hw_truths: God’s love is not a reward for my service.

Christ died for me while I was powerless.
log: Each day, write: “God loves me fully today,” and one way I served out of joy, not pressure.
name_example: For at just the right time, while Sarah was still powerless, Christ died for her.

prayer: Father, thank You that You loved me first, before I ever did anything for You. Help me reject the lie that the more I do for You, the more You love me. Let me rest in Your complete love and serve You out of joy. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
